definition: a vehicle that carries a coffin at a funeral
hook: The hearse began as a farm tool for breaking up soil.
modernAnchor: A long black car moving at walking pace with its headlights on in daylight. We call it a hearse.
journey: A hirpex was a harrow: a heavy triangular frame set with iron teeth, dragged across a field to break the earth.
Old French kept the word as herse. Then somebody noticed that a frame of candles standing over a coffin had the very same shape.
By about 1300 the word had moved to the candle frame, then to the canopy above the tomb, then to the carriage underneath it.
The same root gave English rehearse, to rake over the same ground again, which is exactly what a rehearsal is.
